summary:
--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Given no noise, deterministic strategies." and "We can design a strategy that is generally nice but can exploit naive cooperators and punish defectors."
STRATEGY: Parent slot 0 is a cooperative/forgiving strategy with fitness 257.44. The trace simulates the 11 listed opponents (always C, always D, TFT-like, forgiving, grudge-holding, exploitative) and considers testing/exploiting always C. It plans to revise by adding opponent modeling, early probing, and endgame defection while avoiding catastrophic retaliation.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "So a strategy that never defects first (i.e., always cooperates until opponent defects, then retaliates) would score:" / "So a purely cooperative-until-defected strategy scores 300 against 10 opponents, and ~99 against always D."
STRATEGY: The parent is a complex strategy with forgiveness/retaliation logic; the trace simulates the population of opponent strategies (slots 1-11) and traces their responses to defection; it proposes a modified TFT that never defects first, with endgame defection at round 100, to avoid triggering grudge holders like slot 5.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice suggests forgiveness after a temporary disruption." / "The general advice says forgive after a temporary disruption. So we should forgive a single defection if the opponent has been mostly cooperative."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy using opp_coop_rate/recent_rate, forgiving a single defection when opp_coop_rate > 0.7 and n > 5, retaliating on defection, and cooperating when opp_coop_rate > 0.85. The trace simulates it against slot 7 (periodic defector), slot 5 (end-game grudge), slot 8 (always D), slot 1 (always C), and slot 10 (exploits high cooperation), and proposes adding a consecutive-defection rule, raising the forgiveness threshold to 0.8, and always defecting at the final round.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's write a new strategy based on the parent, with these improvements"
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates, forgives single defections, retaliates on defection, defects late. Simulated against 11 slots (always C, TFT, always D, slot 5, slot 7, slot 10, etc.). Changed by adding last-round defection (n==99), consecutive-D retaliation, and an n==16 rule targeting slot 10's first defection.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the strategy seems robust and improved. Let's write the final code."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates initially, forgives isolated defections when opponent cooperation rate is high, retaliates after consecutive defections, and defects at the final round. Simulated against TFT, slot 5, slot 10, and random defectors. Changed by adding a special-case defection at n==16 for an opponent whose first defection follows all-cooperation, plus final-round defection at n==99.
